content:
The test image shows a corn ear with dark blue-green/teal colored mold growing extensively between and on kernels. Key observations:
- Dark green/teal mold covering large portions of the ear
- Kernels still visible beneath the mold growth
- Mold appears between kernel rows

Top candidates: **Ear_rots_Trichoderma** (dark green mold on/between kernels) or **Ear_rots_Aspergillus** (olive-green powdery mold, typically at tip).

Let me view reference images for both, plus Ear_rots_Gibberella for comparison.

The Trichoderma reference images are an almost perfect match to the test image — dark teal-green mold growing between and on kernels with the same distinctive coloring and pattern. The Aspergillus reference shows more olive/gray-green powdery mold with very different appearance.

Let me view one more reference for confidence.

Diplodia shows white/grayish-brown mold — clearly different from the test image. The Trichoderma match is conclusive: the test image shows the characteristic dark blue-green mold growing between kernels on the upper portion of the ear, with the lower kernels still visible and relatively intact.

{"prediction": "Ear_rots_Trichoderma", "confidence": 0.93, "reasoning": "The test image shows dark teal/blue-green mold growing extensively between and on corn kernels, which is the hallmark of Trichoderma ear rot. The color and growth pattern exactly match the Trichoderma reference collage images — dark green mold coating kernel surfaces and filling spaces between rows. This contrasts clearly with Aspergillus (olive-green powdery mold at tip), Diplodia (white/gray-brown mold from base), and Gibberella (pink/red mold from tip)."}
